html:
The Huetar were the main people of the central valley and Caribbean slopes of Costa Rica when the Spanish arrived in the 1500s. They spoke a Chibchan language and lived in chiefdoms, growing maize, beans and cacao, and they traded with the Chorotega of the Pacific side.

Spanish settlers founded Cartago in the central valley in 1563, and the Huetar were put to work under the encomienda system. One of their chiefs, remembered as Garabito, led resistance in the west. Disease and colonial labour shrank them sharply. Their language is lost, but Huetar communities survive at Quitirrisí and Zapatón. Neighbours: Bribri.
